children.translated_text: Having visualized as before up to the culmination of <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness),
seated upon a white lotus, arisen from the syllable <s>Tāṃ</s>, upon a moon disc,
with legs bound in <s>vajraparyaṅka</s> (adamantine cross-legged posture), holding the <s>varada</s> (boon-granting) gesture and an <s>utpala</s> (blue lotus), // 1 //
in appearance like the rays of the autumn moon, resting upon a moon at the back,
adorned with all ornaments, in the form of a sixteen-year-old maiden, // 2 //
having meditated on the noble <s>Tārā</s>, in her heart a wheel of white radiance,
with eight compartments, filled with eight syllables, // 3 //
with the syllable <s>Oṃ</s> and the <s>hā</s> vowel in the center, and the name of the practitioner beginning at the navel (<s>nābhi</s>),

children.text: dhyāyād ekāgracittaḥ san ṣaṇ māsān dṛḍhaniścayaḥ || 4 ||
children.translated_text: one should meditate with one-pointed mind for six months with firm resolve. // 4 //

body.text: japed akhinnacittaḥ san mantram enaṃ daśākṣaram //
body.translated_text: With unwearied mind, one should recite this ten-syllable <s>mantra</s>:

body.text: tatrāiṣa mantraḥ oṃ tāre tuttāre ture svāhā || 5 ||
body.translated_text: The <s>mantra</s> here is: <s>Oṃ Tāre Tuttāre Ture Svāhā</s>. // 5 //

children.translated_text: One who meditates on the heart-wheel of <s>Tārā</s> shall not be touched by the faults of death,
and shall obtain all <s>siddhis</s> (spiritual attainments) within six months, being devoted to this practice. // 6 //

body.translated_text: The <s>Mṛtyuvañcanatārāsādhana</s> (Practice of <s>Tārā</s> for Cheating Death) (is completed).
